newsitem.title: CANADA: Arakis drills as venture talks continue.
newsitem.headline: Arakis drills as venture talks continue.

text.p: Arakis Energy Corp said on Wednesday that it began drilling the first well of its 1997 exploration program in Sudan.

The company, which is in the midst of negotiations aimed at striking a joint venture deal necessary in developing its 12.2-million acre oil concession and building a pipeline to the Red Sea from southern Sudan, said it started drilling an exploration well at El Saqr on November 23.
The El Saqr well, located 25 km south of the Heglig base camp, is expected to be drilled to a depth of 3,000 metres, Arakis said.
Meanwhile, intense negotiations with prospective deal participants continued today in Sudan, Arakis chief executive John McLeod said in a phone interview from Khartoum.

McLeod has said the company aimed to finalize by the end of this year a deal to develop its Heglig and Unity oil fields, which harbor reserves estimated at 600 million barrels and build the 950-mile pipeline through a joint venture. The estimated cost of the project was US$930 million over 30 months.
The talks were "very positive and the interest is very high," McLeod said.
"We continue to make progress. That's all I can say. We're working hard at it and trying to put it together as quick as we can."
He said Arakis was still hammering out which international oil companies and financial institutions would be in the final deal.

Once the consortium was chosen and its plans finalized, the package would be submitted to the Khartoum government for final approval, he said, adding that changes to Arakis's production sharing agreement would likely be made then.
He would not confirm that changes would include extensions to the time necessary for developing acreage.
